mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in WORKPLACES mobility over the past four weeks indicates reduced commuting and in-person work, which will continue to suppress weekday retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES continuing its declining trend.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests a renewed willingness for out-of-home activities, which will spill over into a modest increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as people combine errands.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the last 14 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM showing a week-on-week increase of more than 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in PARKS mobility from a low point, while RESIDENTIAL activity remains elevated, indicates a shift towards outdoor leisure that will also encourage local retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rebounds by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week from a value below -30%, while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the last 14 days, even with PARKS rebounding from a low and RESIDENTIAL remaining high.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently low and stable TRANSIT station activity indicates a continued reluctance or inability to use public transportation, which will limit access to central retail and recreation areas and keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is significantly higher than over the last 28 days, despite TRANSIT mobility remaining below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility above 10% for the past four weeks indicates a strong preference for staying home, directly limiting opportunities for out-of-home retail and recreation, thus keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to stay above 10%.

mechanism_narrative: High week-to-week volatility in PARKS mobility, potentially driven by unpredictable seasonal weather patterns, creates uncertainty that discourages consistent planning for out-of-home activities, leading to suppressed RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows a clear upward trend despite continued high week-on-week percentage point changes in PARKS mobility (e.g., >10 points).

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in WORKPLACES mobility combined with a sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM activity suggests a shift from work-related outings to local, essential errands, which will provide a slight uplift to local RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks, offsetting some of the workplace decline.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -19% and GROCERY_PHARM stays above 2% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the last 14 days, even if WORKPLACES declines and GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: After a period of persistently low RETAIL_REC, the recent week-on-week rebound suggests a bottoming out and the beginning of a slow recovery, leading to a modest increase in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week after being below -25% for at least two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls back below -25% in the next 7 days, negating the observed rebound.
